A remote that uses every slot with only commands its slot allows, including speaker targets.
A two-bed bedroom config with no scripts or topics; those resolve from the house document by role.
A remote script call is accepted only when the house document declares that script.
A present action that replaces an already presented modal needs sh.modal-handoff@1; Home, weather and climate nodes only accept reject.
A status chip, room tile, weather panel or climate control may only reject a presented modal; replace is not in the app grammar.
pullToRefresh is an optional collection boolean; true adds no capability beyond sh.collection@1.
pullToRefresh false is accepted and the same as omitting it.
pullToRefresh must be a boolean.
The app dropped tonightScript from a bed; unknown keys are rejected.
The app dropped outsideScheduleScript from a bed.
The app dropped scheduleSetTopic; topics resolve from the house document.
The app dropped hotFlashBrokerScript.
The app dropped householdAwayScript.
Any service is accepted since the full-control actions decision (was rejected by the closed per-slot vocabulary: play_media is not a pad-button service).
Any service is accepted since the full-control actions decision (was rejected by the closed per-slot vocabulary: select.select_option is not a pad-button service).
Any service is accepted since the full-control actions decision (was rejected by the closed per-slot vocabulary: media_player.volume_up is not an app-tile service).
Any service is accepted since the full-control actions decision (was rejected by the closed per-slot vocabulary: switch is not an app-tile domain).
Any service is accepted since the full-control actions decision (was rejected by the closed per-slot vocabulary: play_media is not a device-tile service).
Any service is accepted since the full-control actions decision (was rejected by the closed per-slot vocabulary: A page-card command is checked as a device tile).
A target must belong to the called domain.
A script call carries no target.
Any service is accepted since the full-control actions decision (was rejected by the closed per-slot vocabulary: A script the house document does not declare is rejected).
Any service is accepted since the full-control actions decision (was rejected by the closed per-slot vocabulary: Every command of a state action is checked, including conditional cases).
A declared capability the app does not know is rejected before any other mismatch.
The declared capabilities must equal the requirements the document derives.
Schema 1 is gone from the app.
Schema 1 documents are rejected.
The reserved key __proto__ is rejected at any depth.
Two identical keys in one object.
A composed key and its decomposed form are one key after Unicode normalisation.
The same pair in the other order; the second occurrence is reported.
Precomposed and conjoining Hangul are one key.
Keys that are not canonically equivalent are distinct; this fails as an unknown field, not as a duplicate.
A route with only the original fields still decodes; no route-links capability is required.
Routes with aliases, keywords, siri, a viewer-only visibleWhen and linkPrefixes; needs sh.route-links@1 and sh.visible-when@1.
An alias may not equal another route's path: a link must name one route.
An alias is unique across every route.
A route's visibleWhen takes viewer predicates only; viewer-person reads entity state and is refused.
Aliases need sh.route-links@1 in the manifest.
At most eight aliases per route.
siri must be a boolean.
linkPrefixes, when authored, lists at least one slug.
An alias is a plain lower-case path like a route path.
A task page with a resident variant and a list only some users see, shown by a todo collection node.
A grocery page: Add creates an item on one of its own lists.
An admin to-do page whose Add action is the admin form; hidden while Vacation Mode is on.
A defined todo collection no node uses is accepted; it costs nothing.
A todo collection node whose provider no source defines still compiles: the app shows nothing for it and reads no house configuration.
A page lists each entity once.
A list is a todo entity.
An entity id has the form domain.object.
A page has at least one list.
A completion script is a script entity.
The grocery Add action names one of the page's own lists.
The admin Add action names one of the page's own lists.
Add creates a task, a grocery item or an admin to-do.
A list rule names user ids; an administrator rule is not accepted there.
A list rule that also asks for an administrator is not accepted.
A list rule cannot read an entity: a list is read where only the user id is known.
A restricted list stays hidden until the user is known; show and keep are refused.
whenUnknown means nothing without a visibleWhen.
A list says whether completed items are hidden.
The resident variant has a title for the resident and one for everyone else, and nothing more.
A todo collection takes the fields of its schema and no others.
A todo collection has no values to bind; a text cannot read from it.
A document that declares a todo collection must list its capability.
A button calls any domain and service with a literal target and optimistic state.
Any script name and a lock service with an authored confirmation are accepted; the app keeps no allow list.
Call data and target built from every operand kind: read, viewer, format, map, math, list and object.
A bound toggle on a glass tile with on and off calls.
A bound toggle row is allowed in a module list; a bound control without a visibleWhen rule.
A bound slider reads a number attribute and sends the control value.
A bound stepper with a range, a value format and a clamped control value.
A bound choice: each option has its own selectedWhen predicate and call.
A bound button with a confirmation and no control value.
A node shown by a combined predicate (state, viewer, viewer-person, numeric, not) with an explicit unknown policy.
A rule with no whenUnknown keeps the node as it was (the default) and uses any/state only.
A rule hides a child in place in a tile grid and in a plain section.
A navigation tab hidden by a rule.
Local tabs choose their panel from entity state (selectedWhen, first match).
A domain must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$.
A service must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$.
A target key must be entity_id, device_id, area_id, floor_id or label_id.
A literal target must be text or a list of text.
A target key cannot also be a data field.
An optimistic value names a declared source.
An optimistic value needs an ha-entity source, not a model source.
The control value exists only on a bound control's own call.
A call carries no fields beyond the grammar.
A read names a declared source.
A read in an expression needs an ha-entity source.
An ha-entity read path is ["state"] or ["attributes", ...].
A path segment cannot be a prototype name.
The state is text, so it cannot be read as a boolean.
Expressions nest at most eight levels.
A list holds at most 64 items.
A literal text is at most 2,000 characters.
divide takes exactly two arguments.
Every {hole} of a format pattern needs an argument.
There is no template operand and no client-side Jinja.
A viewer fact is userId, isAdmin or personEntityId.
A literal cannot be null.
A predicate names a declared source.
A predicate needs an ha-entity source.
A state predicate lists at least one state.
A numeric predicate needs above or below.
A viewer predicate needs isAdmin or userIds.
all needs at least one predicate.
There is no time predicate yet.
A predicate operand cannot use the control value.
Predicates nest at most eight levels.
whenUnknown means nothing without a visibleWhen.
A module list lets no child go: a visibleWhen on one of its rows is refused.
A paged row lets no child go.
A room section lets no child go.
An automatic rule names one of the local tabs.
A bound toggle needs onAction and offAction.
A toggle sends through onAction and offAction only.
A bound toggle reads isOn.
Only a toggle has a surface.
A stepper's range must be reachable in whole steps.
A stepper format carries a {value} hole.
A slider is the canonical 0 to 100 row and takes no range.
A button has no control value.
Only a bound toggle row, stepper, slider or choice fits a module list.
A saved style over a vacuum with a tile that overrides one state layer by layer.
A library holding the eight built-in styles as saved copies, each with its explicit fallback.
Request settings with pending words, a Home Assistant script and its error timer, and a state action with a confirmation.
A tile with a built-in style and no library: it requires the capability and nothing else.
A style id the library does not define is accepted; the app uses the tile's built-in style.
A library no tile uses is accepted; it costs nothing.
A style with no built-in base on a tile with no built-in style of its own.
An arc override on a state that has no action is accepted.
The arc stands in for the disc, so a rule whose state has an action refuses it.
An unavailable state never shows an arc, so busy and unavailable differ.
The fallback rule follows the same rule about the arc.
A tile's arc override follows the resolved style: the state it names has an action.
With no library style the tile's built-in style decides: a lock's locking state has an action.
`unavailable` and `unknown` are the unknown class in every style.
A library names each style id once.
Every style ends with a fallback rule.
The indicator list is closed.
The colour layer is a palette token, never a value.
The colour layer has two tokens, unlit and lit; a class is never a token.
A colour token is for a resting or in-progress state; a warning keeps the face of its class.
An error keeps the face of its class, so a rule of that class refuses a colour token.
A tile's colour override follows the resolved style: a paused vacuum is a warning and keeps its face.
A state has one of the five classes.
A rule takes the fields of its schema and no others.
A rule names at least one state; the fallback is the rule that names none.
A base is one of the eight built-in styles.
`otherwise` is the same action without a feature, so it needs `requiresFeature`.
The lifecycle names its script and its error timer together.
The lifecycle script is a script entity.
A timing has an upper bound.
A tile names a library style, a built-in style, or both.
A tile's entity is in the domain its style acts on.
A tile's built-in style acts on its own domain.
An entity id has the form domain.object.
An override sets at least one layer.
A tile overrides a state once.
A binding takes the fields of its schema and no others.
A document that carries a style library must list the capability.
